source.title: Impeachment Trial of Vice President Sara Duterte

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: Senate President, the Presiding Officer,

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: and Senator-Judges of the Impeachment Court.

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: The Sergeant at Arms is directed to make a proclamation.

turns.speaker: Alfredo Sotto Corpuz
turns.text: All persons are commanded to keep silent under pain of penalty while the Impeachment Court is in session for the trial of Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte.

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte is hereby called to order. We shall be led in prayer by Senator-Judge Francis Kiko Pangilinan.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan
turns.text: Sa ngalan ng ating Panginoong Diyos, buong kababaang loob na dasal natin na sa lahat ng araw ng impeachment trial, kaliwanagan ng isip, kaayusan sa proseso at pagiging patas at makatarungan. Bilang mga senator-judges na may pagkakataong magtanong sa mga saksi upang linawin ng mga usaping mahalaga sa paglilitis, naway magsilbing gabay sa atin ang mga salita ng Diyos. Sa Proverbs 24.23-24, pinaalalahanan tayo sa bigat ng ating mga pasya. Hindi mabuti ang may kinikilingan sa paghatol. Ang magsabi sa may sala na walang kasalanan ay susumpain ng mga tao at kamumuhian ng mga bansa.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan
turns.text: Ganon din sa mga hahatol doon sa walang sala ng parusa. At sa Proverbs 29.4, pinapaalala sa atin ang bunga ng tunay na katarungan, isang bagay na matagal nang minimiti ng ating bayan. Sa pamamagitan ng katarungan, ang isang pinuno ay nagbibigay ng katatagan sa kanyang bansa. patnubayan n'yo po kami, Panginoon, dito sa aming sagradong tungkulin. Amen.

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: senator-judge, Ontiveros, senator-judge, Lacson, senator-judge, Lapid, senator-judge, Legarda, senator-judge, Marcoleta, senator-judge, Marcos, senator-judge, Padilla, senator-judge, Pangilinan, senator-judge, Sotto III, senator-judge, Tulfo Erwin, senator-judge, Tulfo Raffi, senator-judge, Villanueva, senator-judge, Villar Camil, senator-judge, Villar Marc, senator-judge, Zubiri, the presiding officer, senator-judge, Escudero, Senate President Gachelian.

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: With 16 senator-judges present, the chair declares the presence of a quorum. In accordance with the rules of procedure on impeachment trials, the chair now recognizes the duly elected presiding officer to preside over the proceedings of the impeachment court.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan
turns.text: To correct, we have

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: 17 senator-judges present.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Thank you, Mr. Senate President. If there are no objections, we shall dispense with the reading of the journal. of the Senate, sitting as an impeachment court, dated August 4, 2026, and shall consider the same as approved. The Clerk of Court will please call the case before this impeachment court.

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: Case number 004-2026 in the matter of impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Appearances?

turns.speaker: Rep. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Same appearance for the prosecution, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: For the responded?

turns.speaker: Atty. Michael Wesley Poa
turns.text: Same appearance for the responded accused. Good morning, Your Honors.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Before the chair continues, the Clerk of Court through the Osayas directed to kindly situate the witness at the witness stand for the continuation of his testimony, Mr. Wamil.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Mr. Wamil, I would like to remind you that you will be continuing with your testimony under the same oath that was administered to you the other day. Do you understand that, sir?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Thank you. When we adjourn... The examination of the witness by the counsels for the parties were finished and we will now proceed with the interjections of the senator-judges this morning. And yesterday, we already indicated the sequence of the interjections and questions from the senator-judges. First to make his interjections would be Senator Rafi Tulfo. Sir, you are recognized. You have two minutes and you may proceed when you're ready. Your Honor,

turns.speaker: Rep. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: may

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: I be recognized first? Yes, what is the pleasure of the Honorable Chua?

turns.speaker: Rep. Gerville “Jinky Bitrics” R. Luistro
turns.text: Your Honor, may we request the counsel for the prosecution, Atty. Kapunan, be recognized, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: The counsel for the panel of prosecutors, Atty. Lorna Kapunan, the designated handling counsel for this witness, may situate herself also accordingly.

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honor. Same appearance.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Good morning. Good morning, Atty. Lorna, Sen. Tulfo, Rafi, you may proceed sir when you're ready. You have two minutes, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Huwag muna, Mr. President, Officer, point of order lamang muna to.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Yes, what is your point of order, Honorable Tulfo?

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Kasi kahapon nabanggit na si Atty. Pua, magaling na abogado siya, ay pumunta sa COA, tama, para makipag-usap tungkol dun sa sinasabing audit query. Now, hindi ko pa conflict of interest yun para siya ay mag-represent dito ngayon sa

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: ano natin, pinag-uusapang confidential funds, when in fact, eh siya mismo pumunta doon sa COA office para makipag-uusap sa kanila. What do you think, Mr. President Officer?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: The respondent in this case, Senator-Judge Tulfo, is the Honorable Vice President, Sara Zimmerman Duterte. Attorney Powa, although he served under the office of the Vice President, I believe, and even under DepEd, is not a named respondent to this case. And in fact, is one of the lawyers, as you can see, of the respondent. I believe there is no conflict with respect to that given that he is not. The one in trial in this case.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Okay, I rest my case, Mr. President Officer. Ngayon, pwede nang... Pwede nang simulan ni Annika. Yung oras. Mr. Witness, bukod sa OVP at saka DepEd, we're talking about confidential funds, meron pa pa ibang ahensya ng pamalaan na inaudit nyo ang kanilang confidential funds?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Based on the GAA po, meron may mga other agencies na may allotment for confidential funds.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Kaya nga meron kayo mga na-audit.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yes po, Your

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: At dito sa mga agency na-audit ninyo, magkapareho ba ang utilization nila ng confidential funds sa OBP under BP-SARA and those agencies na inaudit nyo?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yung utilization naman po ng confidential fund ay separate and distinct for every agency since yung kanilang utilization ay based on their mandate or operations.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Okay. Sila ba'y gumamit ng mga aliases, gumamit ng mga pangalan, chichiria, etc.?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yan po ay hindi ko na pwede. Ang alam ko po, hindi ko po mati-determine based on the documents submitted since hindi naman po naka-indicate dun sa kanilang submission na yung mga pangalan na nandun ay aliases or not.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Noong April 2026, nag-issue kayo ng disallowance.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: sa OVP and its officers para at the same time ipinasusuli n'yo yung parte ng confidential funds.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Can you repeat your question, Your Honor?

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: I think that was April of 2025.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Nag-issue kayo nung, pinasusuli n'yo ilang parte ng confidential funds ng OVP.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: I do not have personal knowledge na po about yan since wala na po ako sa ICPAO nung February. 12, 2023 po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Okay. Anong reason ba't pinasusuli yung party ng confidential funds na disallowed? What are the reasons?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Wala po akong personal knowledge about dyan since hindi naman po ako yung nag-issue ng disallowance. Nung na-issue po yung disallowance ay na-transfer na po ako to other agency of DICOA.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: I think it was April 10, 2026. So wala na po kayo doon?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Sinabi kahapon ni Atty. Poa na binagit niya natin yung circular, co-circular ng 1992, if I'm not mistaken, na hindi dapat banggitin yung pangalan ng mga recipient dahil for reasons of security and national security, security ng tao ng recipients and national security.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: It compromised sa tingin po ninyo yung security ng informant kung hihingan nyo sila ng resibo patungkol sa mga gamot na natanggap nila mula sa confidential funds?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Katulad nga po nung sinabi ko during my testimony, ang hinihingi po namin ay yung purop nung pagbili when it comes to the official receipt and the sales invoice po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Correct. Alimbaw, resibo, bumili ng maintenance or antibiotics, yung gano'ng klaseng resibo, dapat iba ang hinihingi n'yo.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yes, po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Pero ang sinasabi nila, eh, yun daw ay magdi-geopardize, magkakaroon ng problema sa national security.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Actually, yung minention po nila na circular, which is yung 1999, is already repealed na. Repealed na. Opo.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Pero just the same. Sa tingin nyo ba, yung pagbibili ng chichiria o dili kayo pagbili ng shampoo o suka sa sari-sari store, would that jeopardize the national security kapag yan ay binulugan sa inyo, binigyan ka ng simo?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Hindi po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Thank you.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Thank you, Senator-Judge Rafi Tulfo. Next to make his interjections would be Senator Bam Aquino. You are recognized, sir. You may proceed when you're ready. You have two minutes.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Maraming salamat, Mr. Presiding Officer. Attorney, good morning. Good morning po, Senator. So, ang common understanding po kasi ng confidential funds ay secret, puwedeng gamitin sa kung ano-ano, hindi pwedeng i-bulgar sa publiko. Hindi po totoo, no? Meron po talagang rules and regulations sa paggamit ng confidential funds.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yes.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Were you already part of the ICFAO in 2015?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yes po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: So yung pinakitang memo noong 1992 at itong memo na pinag-usapan natin na circa 2015, parang magkaibang magkaiba siya, no?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Do you know the reason why the rules changed with regard to the usage of confidential funds?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Since yung paggamit po noong confidential fund at intelligence fund ay kailangan ng strict accounting and auditing rules. Nagkaroon po ng circular para ma-ensure na yung paggamit po ay properly accounted at hindi po magamit for personal use or misuse.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Yan yung laman ng memo. Pero ang tanong ko, do you know why it was changed? Kasi parang lumalabas magkaiba yung paggamit nito if you look at the 1992 circular, iba sa 2015.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Doon po kasi sa yung Circular ng 1999, walang differentiation as to the CIF po. Pero doon sa 2015-01 kasi doon na in-specify na dapat yung Confidential Fund ay gagamitin lang sa ganito for civilian government agencies. Yung Intelligence Fund ay gagamitin lang ng uniform and military personnel as well as yung mga intelligence practitioners.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Kung baga ang dilinaw noong 2015 Circular yung paggamit at pag-liquidate?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: And is there a new circular after 2015 or ito pa rin yung ginagamit ninyo?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yan pa rin po yung ginagamit, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Okay, second question. Anong pinagkaiba ng AR sa OR? Ang OR po kasi,

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: ini-issue po siya nung mga pinagbilan na BIR registered. So, yung AR naman po, yun yung ginagamit ng agency para prove na binigay nila yung payment or payment dun sa tao na naka-receive noong payment.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: And it seems na mas katanggap-tanggap sa inyo yung OR kesa AR. Is that correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Depende po yan, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Kapag purchases po kasi, kailangan po talagang OR yung ibigay sa amin kasi doon po namin tinitignan kung nag-purchase po talaga sila.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Kasi official receipt, acknowledgement receipt, sabihin ng tao, pareho namang resibo, parehong receipt. Ano pinagkaya ba niya?

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Yung

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: acknowledgement receipt

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: po kasi, ina-acknowledge doon nung recipient ng payment na natanggap niya yung payment. Pero yung OR po kasi, parang yun yung proof na nag-purchase si agency doon sa pinagbila nung item.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Nung item. So pwede mong matrace? Kung OR, pwede nyo matrace?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Kung AR, pwede nyo po ba itong matrace o hindi na?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Pag-AR po kasi, kung ano lang po talaga yung nandun sa face nung document, yun lang po yung basis namin since document-based po yung audit namin. Pag-AR po kasi, makikita lang po doon kung saan binili. Okay, yun lang yung information. Tsaka kung sino ang

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: tumanggap?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Opo, yung pinagbilan po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Okay, dito naman sa tumatanggap, allowed ba yung code names? Allowed ba yung alias sa inyo?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Based on the provision of the joint circular, it is neither allowed nor prohibited po since silent po yung joint circular as to that.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Is that as of 2015 or even in previous liquidation of confidential funds?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Based on my recollection po, even yung dating circulars po, buwat nung nag-assume po ako sa IGFA, wala naman pong provision as to the use of alias.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: So bawal ang

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: paggamit ng alias?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: The circular is silent po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Okay. Para sa inyo, kung alias... Yung paggamit ng alias ay bawal. So, hindi importante kung may ibang tao ito, totoong tao ba ito. Basta yung pangalan na binigay sa inyo, ang expectation nyo, totoong tao yan. Based on that, kasi

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: ang katulad nga po nung sinabi ko, document-based po kami. So, wala po kaming way to determine if this is an alias or not.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: But in general, ang tinatanggap yung dokumento, dapat totoong tao.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Okay, next. Did you have any, napag-usapan n'yo kahapon yung dealings n'yo with OVP nung lumabas na or malapit nang lumabas yung AOM. Previous to that, meron ka bang dealings with OVP?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Wala na po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: So wala kang, walang kumausap sa inyo, walang nagtanong kung paano to dapat i-liquidate apart from the meeting which included Atty. Powa?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Wala na po akong maalala, Your Honor. Last

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: question lang, Mr. Presiding Officer. Please wind up.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Yung notice, yung AOM, ibig sabihin yan, may chance na pa kayong i-correct, di ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yes, for Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Pag notice of disallowance na, may chance pa ba yung i-correct o naniningil na?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Actually, the moment that we issue notice of disallowance, nirequire na po yung accountable officers to restitute po yung amount involved. And

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: to

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: your

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: knowledge, is there a notice of disallowance for the OVP and DepEd funds?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Wala pong personal knowledge.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: pero nakita ko po sa news po, so I was made aware na may ending na po yung OVP 2022.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: So may notice of disallowance na ang OVP for the 500 million pesos?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: For 125 million pesos po for the fourth quarter of 2022.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: So sinisingil na yan kay Vice President Duterte?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yes po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Thank you, Senator-Judge Aquino. Next to make his interjections is Senator-Judge Pangalinan, your recognizer. You may proceed when you're ready. Thank you, Mr.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan
turns.text: President. Mr. Presiding Officer, magandang umaga, Mr. Witness, ginong mawil.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Marami na po. Sa NDAs po, parang nasa 30 plus na po yung na-audit ko. And sa LDOs, marami na rin po. Hindi ko na po mabilang kung ilang agencies

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: na po yung na-audit ko.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan
turns.text: So, more than 30?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yes po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan
turns.text: Okay. Sa mga ahensya na ito, tatlong pong ahensya, masasabi mo ba na nire-require din yung liquidation ng official receipts at ng sales invoice?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yes po, Your Honor, kasi yung requirement po ng circular ay in-enforce po namin sa lahat ng agencies na inaudit po namin.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan
turns.text: So sa 2022, from December 21 to December 31, ilang sales invoice o kaya official receipt ang kasama dun sa mga liquidation report?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Wala po sinabit sa amin, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan
turns.text: 849 acknowledgement receipts, tama?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yes po, Your Honor. Since ina-apply naman po namin uniformly yung provisions po noong Joint Circular 2015-01.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan
turns.text: As in, puro AR ang sinasubmit ng ibang ahensya?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: May mga agencies po na nagsasubmit naman ng OR po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan
turns.text: So sa experience mo dun sa December 21 to 31, masasabi mo bang standard practice yan ng iba pang mga ahensyang iyong na audit?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Hindi ko po siyang masasabing standard practice since ito po yung kauna-unang beses na puro AR po yung sinamit sa amin.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan
turns.text: So first time sa iyong... 10 years na puro AR lang at walang sales invoice at walang official receipt.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Opo, ganun.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: po kadaming AR kaagad yung sinabi.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan
turns.text: At 125 million na walang sales invoice at walang official receipt.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Yes po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan
turns.text: Doon naman sa usapin ng kung walang sales invoice at walang official receipt, masasabi mo ba na halimbawa yung sa medicines, talagang medicines ang ginasta?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil

turns.speaker: Sen. Panfilo “Ping” M. Lacson

turns.speaker: Sen. Panfilo “Ping” M. Lacson

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil

turns.speaker: Sen. Panfilo “Ping” M. Lacson

turns.text: link between the success and the information

turns.speaker: Sen. Panfilo “Ping” M. Lacson

turns.text: Wala pa po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Isn't it correct na nandun lang sa notice of disallowance yan?

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil
turns.text: Based on the joint circular po, doon po nirequire po na mag-restitute.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Sa notice of disallowance na. Wala sa AOM, walang demand sa notice of suspension sa notice of disallowance.

turns.speaker: Atty. Roderick C. Wamil

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Your Honor. So, when will the presumption come in? under paragraph 8.3. Kung wala pang failure to liquidate, dahil hindi pa final, kung wala pa yung demand until notice of disallowance na hindi pa final, kailan po papasok yung presumption o prima facie doon sa 8.3?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero

turns.text: So pag hiningi nyo at hindi po nasubmit failure na yun sa palagay mo?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan
turns.text: Okay. At hindi kayo pumayag?

turns.text: Yes po, since wala naman po siya doon sa aming Joint Circular, Your Honor.

turns.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Presiding Officer. Magandang umaga po, attorney. Good morning po, Your Honor. Ito, broad strokes lang po ito, Mr. Presiding Officer, to my dear colleagues kasi

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan
turns.text: Sa iyong pananaw, dito sa findings ninyo, napapakita ba na may possibility of misuse and abuse of government funds on confidential and intelligence funds?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: And after considering the objections of the chair of the respondent, the objection is hereby denied subject to the following guidelines. and reasonings. Section 34, Rule 132 of the Rules of Court provide the court shall consider no evidence which has not been presented or formally offered. The purpose for which the evidence is offered must be specified accordingly. The marking, identification, or authentication of a document does not mean that the document has been formally offered or admitted for the purpose it was so stated. The physical transfer of an exhibit designation from a provisional copy to its corresponding original or certified true copy is even more limited. It is a mechanical and ministerial act intended only to maintain the orderly identification of the Court's records. The respondent is not prejudiced by this transfer. The transfer does not alter the substance or evidentiary status of the document . It does not constitute a ruling on the authenticity, admissibility, or evidentiary weight and it does not enlarge the purpose for which the document was originally marked. The respondent therefore loses no substantive or procedural right by reason of the transfer and may raise all appropriate objections when the document is formally offered. This conclusion is consistent with the prosecution's own representation during the July 21, 2026 hearing wherein the Honorable Luistro stated, quote, Your Honor, the document is being presented only to seek confirmation from the witness. that he is referring to this particular document as part of the investigation of the Special Task Force. We are not presenting it to prove the truthfulness of the contents of the affidavit. The Chair likewise previously ruled, quote, Again, this is only as to the fact that this is what the NBI used in their open investigation and coming up with their findings, not as to the truth of the statements being read by Director Matibag. Close quotation. The Chair further clarified on even date, July 21, 2026. The Chair will cut short any further identifications of the witness in regard to this affidavit. This is only as to the fact that Las Cañas executed a document that they used in their open source investigation, not as to the truth of what was said. The limitations remain controlling even after the transfer of the marking of this exhibit to a certified true copy. Exhibits P-4-35, 35A, and 35B remain merely independently relevant statements only to establish that the document came to the attention of and was used by the NBI in its investigation. It may not be used as proof of the truth of the allegations stated therein. As stated in Espinelli v. People, GR No. 79-535, dated 6-9-14, when the relevant fact is merely that a statement was made, the hearsay rule does not bar proof of that fact, regardless of the statement's truth or falsity. Finally, the transfer of the markings does not cure the defects already placed on the record. turns.text: The court acting on the motion for judicial notice dated August 3, seeking judicial notice of the existence and official character of the hearings and the corresponding transcripts or judicial recordings and the committee report identified therein.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Section 1, Rule 129 of the Rules Provide, a court shall take judicial notice without need of the introduction of evidence of legislative, executive, and judicial departments of the National Government of the Philippines. As stated in CLT, the case cited by the counsel for the prosecutors, there is such, referring to a Senate Committee report, The court took judicial notice of the Senate committee report but only as to the existence of the committee report and not as to the content and truth of what was stated in the committee report. Therefore, accordingly, the court grants the requested judicial notice to be taken by the court but solely and exclusively limited to the following facts. Number one, that the legislative hearings were actually held. and under the official function of the House of Representatives Committee on Good Government and Public Accountability and the Committee on Justice. So to reiterate, just as to the factual existence that the hearings were indeed conducted. Number two, that the corresponding transcripts, official audiovisual recordings and committee report exist. As official records of the proceedings and in a separate rule, therefore enjoy the regularity of official proceedings absent contrary proof that there is either fraud, falsity, or inaccuracy, therefore which will overcome the presumption of regularity. With a warning. Having granted the motion, only within the foregoing limits, the chair now states in unmistakable terms the precise effect of this ruling and reminds the prosecution, and should the time come, also the respondent, if they happen to cross this line also, Rule

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: 129 is captioned, What need not be proved. Therefore, the court states with precision what the prosecution need not prove, only with respect to those two things. Nothing else is judicially admitted or established. The prosecution is therefore expressly reminded that judicial notice shall not be used as a vehicle to place into the record substantive contents of the transcripts, recordings, or committee reports. It is not a substitute for the presentation and formal offer of competent evidence, nor does it dispense with the applicable rules on authentication, hearsay, relevance, and the right of the respondent to object and confront the evidence presented against her. As the Supreme Court held in Magkamit v. IAS, PIDEA, GR No. 19-8-140-125-16, fair play requires. that the respondent be given meaningful opportunity to rebut all the evidence presented against her. Therefore, consistent with the Chair's prior ruling on July 21 in relation to the Las Cañas document, a witness will not hereafter be allowed to read in open court a third-party statement that is not his or her own, as the respondent would be denied the opportunity to rebut those statements and cross-examine. The statements made by a third party.
